media_work.focus_or_theme: Examines the experiences of crime victims and their family members when the person convicted of the crime is later exonerated

media_item.case_details_raw: While specific case details are not provided, the book presents original crime victims' experiences with violent crime, investigations and trials, and later exonerations.  It includes in-depth interviews with 21 crime victims across the US, revealing the impact of primary (original crime), secondary (investigations and trials), and tertiary (wrongful convictions and exonerations) trauma. The book explores how victims process these traumas, focusing on challenges faced when the convicted person is exonerated.
key_quotes_raw: "With this book, Cook gives voice to the original crime victims of wrongful convictions and their family members whose experiences of surviving trauma and navigating the criminal legal system have been largely ignored." (from publisher description)
"Shattered Justice presents original crime victims' experiences with violent crime, investigations and trials, and later exonerations in their cases." (from publisher description)

media_item.summary_notes: "Shattered Justice: Crime Victims' Experiences with Wrongful Convictions and Exonerations" by Kimberly J. Cook offers a unique perspective by focusing on the experiences of original crime victims and their families in cases with wrongful convictions and later exonerations.  The book, based on interviews with 21 crime victims, details the primary (original crime), secondary (investigations and trials), and tertiary (exoneration) trauma experienced. It explores themes of grief, loss, healing, and repair, advocating for restorative justice practices and policy reforms to prevent and mitigate the harms of wrongful convictions.
